trust_decision.summary: Every path the installer reads or copies for a skill must stay inside the fetched skill tree; the decision is enforced both where the tree is walked (Discovery::find_skills follows symlinks) and where it is recursively copied (copy_dir_all dereferences entries and the skill root itself).

landing_point.why: The advisory says `skilo add` follows symbolic links; the only place `add` turns a skill directory into installed files is copy_dir_all, where fs::read_dir at :576 recurses through a linked directory and fs::copy at :585 dereferences a linked file.

fix_sites.entry_point: Discovery::find_skills (public, re-exported at src/skill/mod.rs:16) called from src/commands/add.rs:389; also used by lint/fmt/to-prompt/read-properties
fix_sites.module_kind: shared library helper (src/skill, not the add command)

fix_sites.entry_point: Discovery::find_skills fast path returns root/SKILL.md when it exists, without checking whether the directory or the manifest is a symlink
fix_sites.module_kind: shared library helper (src/skill, not the add command)

fix_sites.entry_point: skilo add (CLI subcommand, dispatched at src/main.rs:16)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Discovery has followed symlinks by design since the first ADR (docs/adr/0002-rust-implementation.md:713) and is shared by lint, fmt, to-prompt and read-properties, so it is a deliberate general-purpose helper and only the copy inside commands/add.rs needs a guard.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The installer must keep copying a skill's real optional subdirectories recursively (scripts/, references/, assets/) and discovery must keep resolving user-built symlinked skill layouts; a blanket 'skip every entry whose metadata is not a plain file/dir' or 'refuse the whole tree if any symlink exists' fix silently drops legitimate skill content.

O6_input_shapes: symlink to a file inside the skill directory (fs::copy at src/commands/add.rs:585 dereferences and copies the target's bytes into the install directory)
symlink to a directory inside the skill directory (entry.file_type().is_dir() is false for the link, so it reaches fs::copy, which fails, while a recursion-through variant reaches fs::read_dir)
skill directory that is itself a symlink, returned by the follow_links walk and then passed whole as the src argument at src/commands/add.rs:560
manifest path reached through a symlinked directory by WalkDir::follow_links at src/skill/discovery.rs:45

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The skill directory itself is a symlink: Discovery returns root/link/SKILL.md, install_skills passes the symlink as src to copy_dir_all, and the per-entry check never applies to the root, so fs::read_dir recurses into the external directory.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The skill root is selected by discovery or by the user's own source argument, not by the malicious repository; only entries inside the skill look attacker-controlled, so guarding the entry loop is enough.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file (commands/add.rs) plus the discovery walker one module away

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Fallback discovery under root/skills and root/<agent skills dir> runs the same follow_links walk when nothing is found at the source root, so a repository can ship a symlinked skills/ directory pointing at a local tree.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is only a convenience fallback that runs when no SKILL.md exists at the source root, so it is a secondary path a fix to the main install need not cover.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different function from the copy sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A `--link` install mode that symlinks the cached checkout's skill directory into the agent skills dir instead of copying it.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Package managers commonly offer link/editable installs to avoid copies, and add already has an alternative destination route (--output); such a mode re-introduces the same containment question in the opposite direction.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Installing straight from the materialised checkout (or from tree blobs in the bare repo) without the copy step.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: fetch already materialises the tree via git2 checkout_tree, which honours symlink entries; a maintainer could skip the duplicate copy as an optimisation and inherit the same symlink tree.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Removal of an installed skill that is a symlink, via remove_dir_all on the skill path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: remove was written next to add and follows the same 'skill name -> directory' assumption, so a maintainer extending install semantics would plausibly leave removal symmetric and unguarded.

O9_family: CWE-59 / CWE-61 link following leading to arbitrary local file disclosure (CWE-200)

O10_build.toolchain: cargo; rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.92.0 (Cargo.toml rust-version 1.85); git2 vendored-libgit2 builds libgit2 from source, so a C compiler is needed
O10_build.project_tests: 43 inline #[cfg(test)] unit tests across 9 files (e.g. src/skill/discovery.rs:105-338, src/commands/add.rs:597-631); no tests/ integration directory; none of them exercise copy_dir_all or symlinks, and the git test at src/git/fetch.rs:429-431 is marked #[ignore] for network use

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a file_type()?.is_symlink() skip inside copy_dir_all's entry loop only, which still copies a skill directory that is itself a symlink and leaves Discovery's follow_links(true) in place.

out_of_scope_notes: skilo fmt reads and rewrites a discovered SKILL.md in place (src/commands/fmt.rs:44, src/commands/fmt.rs:62), so a symlinked manifest is an arbitrary-file overwrite rather than the advisory's disclosure; noted, not pursued.

skilo lint's script rules read files under scripts/ through read_dir and read_to_string (src/skill/rules/scripts.rs:25, src/skill/rules/scripts.rs:89); content is only tested for a shebang, outside the advisory's install/disclosure path, not pursued.
skilo remove calls remove_dir_all on an installed skill path (src/commands/remove.rs:119); same link-following family but outside this advisory's read/disclosure scope, not pursued.
